sounds.name: Funk Bass
sounds.ref: A round bass that snaps bright and settles dark, the ARP sound of Herbie Hancock’s “Chameleon” bassline
sounds.blurb: A round, snapping bass: two oscillators through a closed filter that the ADSR flicks open on every note.
sounds.how: VCO-2’s pulse joins VCO-1’s sawtooth, a hair out of tune, for weight. The filter sits low with some resonance, and the ADSR opens it with a quick decay, so each note starts with a bright snap and settles dark.

steps.title: Two oscillators
steps.why:
Bring in VCO-2 on its pulse beside VCO-1’s sawtooth, and pull it slightly out of tune.
- Mixer VCO-2 7 · 70%
- Mixer VCO-2 wave VCO-2 pulse
- VCO-2 FINE 5.4 · +0.2 st
- Listen for: a fuller note with a slow beat in it.

steps.title: Close the filter
steps.why:
Switch to the 4035 and bring the cutoff down, with a little resonance.
- VCF MODE 4-POLE (4035)
- VCF FREQ 3.5 · 180 Hz
- VCF RESONANCE 4 · 40%
- Listen for: a dark, muffled bass with a slight hum at the cutoff.

steps.title: The snap
steps.why:
Let the ADSR open the filter on each note and close it again quickly.
- VCF ADSR or AR 6 · 60%
- ADSR ATTACK 0 · 5 ms
- ADSR DECAY 3.5 · 110 ms
- ADSR SUSTAIN 2 · 20%
- ADSR RELEASE 1 · 29 ms
- Listen for: a bright bite at the front of each note that falls straight back.

context.vcf.freq: How dark the bass sits between notes.
context.vcf.env: How bright the snap at the start of each note is.

tweaks.hear: A rubbery, quacking bass.
A slower, more vocal wah on every note.

sounds.name: Sync Sweep Lead
sounds.ref: A tearing, vocal sync lead swept on every note, close to George Duke’s Odyssey solos with Frank Zappa
sounds.blurb: A tearing, vocal lead: VCO-2 synced to VCO-1, its pitch swept by the ADSR on every note.
sounds.how: With SYNC on, VCO-2 restarts with each cycle of VCO-1, so it plays VCO-1’s pitch and its own pitch changes the tone instead. The ADSR pushes VCO-2’s pitch up at the start of each note and lets it fall, sweeping the harmonics.

steps.title: Sync VCO-2
steps.why:
Hear VCO-2 alone, synced to VCO-1, and raise its pitch.
- Mixer VCO-1 0 · 0%
- Mixer VCO-2 9 · 90%
- VCO-2 SYNC on
- VCO-2 COARSE 7 · 502 Hz (B4 at C4)
- Listen for: the note still at VCO-1’s pitch, but hard and nasal.

steps.title: Sweep it
steps.why:
Switch VCO-2’s second FM slider to the ADSR and raise it.
- VCO-2 FM source (S/H or ADSR) ADSR
- VCO-2 FM (S/H or ADSR) 6 · 17.3 st
- ADSR DECAY 5 · 320 ms
- ADSR SUSTAIN 3 · 30%
- Listen for: each note opening with a tearing sweep that settles.

steps.title: Take the edge off
steps.why:
Bring the cutoff down a little.
- VCF FREQ 7.5 · 2.8 kHz
- VCF RESONANCE 2 · 20%
- Listen for: the same sweep, less harsh at the top.

steps.title: Vibrato and glide
steps.why:
A touch of the LFO on VCO-1 (VCO-2 follows it through the sync), and a little portamento.
- VCO-1 FM (LFO) 2.5 · ±0.8 st
- LFO FREQ 6 · 3.17 Hz
- PORTAMENTO 2 · 120 ms
- Listen for: a singing lead that slides between notes.

context.vco2.sync: Locks VCO-2 to VCO-1: the source of the tearing tone.
context.vco2.fm2: How far the ADSR sweeps VCO-2 at the start of each note.
context.vco2.coarse: Where the sweep settles: the tone of the held note.

tweaks.hear: A brighter, more metallic held note.
A wilder, longer sweep on every note.

sounds.name: Duophonic Fifths
sounds.ref: Two keys, two oscillators: gliding intervals through one filter, for 1970s progressive rock leads
sounds.blurb: Two notes at once: hold two keys and each VCO takes one, gliding as the pair moves.
sounds.how: The ODYSSEY is duophonic: VCO-1 plays the lowest key held and VCO-2 the highest. With both in the mixer, a pair of keys sounds as an interval, through one filter and one envelope.

steps.title: Bring in VCO-2
steps.why:
Raise VCO-2 in the mixer, then hold two keys.
- Mixer VCO-2 9 · 90%
- Listen for: two notes at once, VCO-1 on the lower key and VCO-2 on the upper.

steps.title: Shape the tone
steps.why:
Darken the filter and let the ADSR open it a little on each note.
- VCF FREQ 6.5 · 1.4 kHz
- VCF RESONANCE 3 · 30%
- VCF ADSR or AR 3 · 30%
- ADSR DECAY 4 · 160 ms
- ADSR SUSTAIN 5 · 50%
- Listen for: a warmer pair with a soft attack.

steps.title: Glide between
steps.why:
Add portamento: both VCOs slide to their new keys.
- PORTAMENTO 3 · 270 ms
- Listen for: the interval sliding from one pair of keys to the next.

context.mixer.vco2: VCO-2 is the upper note of the pair.

tweaks.hear: Only the top note of each pair.
Both keys at the lower pitch, the upper one now changing the tone.

sounds.name: Ring-Mod Bells
sounds.ref: Clanging, inharmonic ring-mod bells that ring on after each key, out of a 1970s science-fiction score
sounds.blurb: Clanging, inharmonic bells from the ring modulator, ringing away after each key.
sounds.how: The ring modulator multiplies VCO-1’s and VCO-2’s pulses. With VCO-2 tuned to an awkward interval above VCO-1, the result has tones that belong to neither: a bell. The AR’s long release lets each strike ring.

steps.title: The ring modulator
steps.why:
Switch the first mixer channel to RING MOD and raise it; take VCO-1 out of the mixer.
- Mixer NOISE or RING MOD RING MOD
- NOISE or RING MOD 9 · 90%
- Mixer VCO-1 0 · 0%
- Listen for: no bell yet: with both VCOs on the same pitch there is nothing for them to clash with.

steps.title: Tune them apart
steps.why:
Move VCO-2 to an awkward interval above VCO-1.
- VCO-2 COARSE 7.2 · 551 Hz (C♯5 at C4)
- VCO-1 PULSE WIDTH 3 · 37%
- Listen for: a clangorous, metallic tone that no longer sounds one clear pitch.

steps.title: Let it ring
steps.why:
Give the AR a long release, and let it close the filter as the note dies.
- AR RELEASE 7 · 1.3 s
- VCF envelope (ADSR or AR) AR
- VCF ADSR or AR 4 · 40%
- VCF FREQ 6.5 · 1.4 kHz
- Listen for: each strike ringing on and softening as it fades.

context.mixer.noise_ring_src: RING MOD: the two VCOs multiplied.
context.vco2.coarse: The interval between the VCOs decides the bell’s colour.

tweaks.hear: A different, darker bell.
The bell collapses: synced, the VCOs no longer beat against each other.

sounds.name: Sample and Hold Burble
sounds.ref: Random filter steps ticking at the LFO’s rate: the computer-at-work burble of 1970s science fiction
sounds.blurb: The computer-at-work sound: random steps of the filter, ticking at the LFO’s rate.
sounds.how: The S/H mixer starts with the noise at full, and the sample and hold reads it on each LFO cycle: a new random value every tick. On the filter’s S/H slider, with resonance, each value is a new burbling note.

steps.title: Random steps into the filter
steps.why:
Bring the cutoff down, raise the resonance, and raise the filter’s S/H slider.
- VCF FREQ 4.5 · 358 Hz
- VCF RESONANCE 7 · 70%
- VCF S/H or LFO 6 · 60%
- Listen for: the filter jumping to a new random place twice a second.

steps.title: Speed up the clock
steps.why:
The LFO clocks the sample and hold: raise it.
- LFO FREQ 7.5 · 6.32 Hz
- Listen for: a fast, chattering burble; the RATE light flickers with it.

steps.title: Smooth it a little
steps.why:
OUTPUT LAG rounds off each step.
- OUTPUT LAG 3 · 15 ms
- Listen for: the steps blurring into quick slides.

context.vcf.mod2: How far the random steps move the cutoff.
context.lfo.freq: How often a new step comes.
context.snh.mix2: Noise in the S/H mixer is what makes the steps random.

tweaks.hear: VCO-1 joins the noise in the S/H mixer: the steps fall into patterns.
Each step whistles: a random melody.

sounds.name: LFO Repeat Pulse
sounds.ref: One held key turned into a run of plucks by the LFO, a Berlin School pulse with no sequencer
sounds.blurb: One held key becomes a run of pulses: the LFO fires the AR over and over.
sounds.how: With the AR on LFO REPEAT, the LFO square triggers it on every cycle while a key is down (KYBD REPEAT). The AR also opens the filter, so every pulse is a pluck, and VCO-2 an octave up brightens it.

steps.title: Repeat the AR
steps.why:
Switch the AR to LFO REPEAT and set the LFO’s speed. Hold a key.
- AR KYBD GATE or LFO REPEAT LFO REPEAT
- LFO FREQ 6.5 · 3.99 Hz
- AR RELEASE 3 · 79 ms
- Listen for: a steady stream of notes from one held key, stopping when you let go.

steps.title: A pluck on every pulse
steps.why:
Let the AR open the filter as well.
- VCF FREQ 4 · 254 Hz
- VCF RESONANCE 5 · 50%
- VCF envelope (ADSR or AR) AR
- VCF ADSR or AR 5 · 50%
- Listen for: each pulse a short, resonant pluck.

steps.title: An octave above
steps.why:
Add VCO-2 an octave up.
- Mixer VCO-2 6 · 60%
- VCO-2 COARSE 7.09 · 524 Hz (C5 at C4)
- Listen for: a brighter, ringing pulse.

context.repeat.ar: LFO REPEAT: the LFO fires the AR, not the key.

tweaks.hear: The pulses carry on with no key held.
A fast, buzzing ripple.

sounds.name: PWM Strings
sounds.ref: Slow, shimmering strings from two moving pulse widths, for the string lines of synth-pop
sounds.blurb: A slow, shimmering string sound from two pulse waves whose widths move with the LFO.
sounds.how: Both VCOs on their pulse, narrowed a little, with the LFO sine moving each width: the pulse width modulation that sounds like an ensemble. The ADSR takes over the loudness, with a slow attack and release.

steps.title: Two pulses
steps.why:
Switch both mixer channels to the pulse and bring in VCO-2, slightly detuned.
- Mixer VCO-1 wave VCO-1 pulse
- Mixer VCO-2 8 · 80%
- Mixer VCO-2 wave VCO-2 pulse
- VCO-2 FINE 5.3 · +0.1 st
- Listen for: a hollow, reedy tone.

steps.title: Move the widths
steps.why:
Narrow each pulse a little and let the LFO sine sweep its width.
- VCO-1 PULSE WIDTH 3 · 37%
- VCO-2 PULSE WIDTH 3 · 37%
- VCO-1 PULSE WIDTH MOD 5 · 50%
- VCO-2 PULSE WIDTH MOD 5 · 50%
- LFO FREQ 3.5 · 1.00 Hz
- Listen for: a slow, shimmering movement, like several players at once.

steps.title: Swell in, fade away
steps.why:
Give the loudness to the ADSR, slow at both ends, and soften the filter.
- VCA envelope (AR or ADSR) ADSR
- ADSR ATTACK 6.5 · 450 ms
- ADSR DECAY 6 · 630 ms
- ADSR SUSTAIN 8 · 80%
- ADSR RELEASE 6.5 · 1.0 s
- VCF FREQ 6.5 · 1.4 kHz
- Listen for: each chord swelling in and dying away after the keys come up.

context.vco1.pwm: How far the LFO moves VCO-1’s width: the shimmer.
context.adsr.attack: How slowly each chord swells in.

tweaks.hear: A faster, more nervous shimmer.
A softer, darker string.

sounds.name: Filter Whistle
sounds.ref: The filter ringing on its own and played in tune, a pure whistle heard all over 1970s library music
sounds.blurb: No oscillators at all: the filter ringing on its own, played in tune from the keys.
sounds.how: At full RESONANCE the 4-pole filter oscillates by itself as a sine. With the VCOs out of the mixer and KYBD CV at full, the keys move the cutoff a semitone a key, so the whistle plays in tune. The LFO on the cutoff gives it vibrato.

steps.title: Silence the VCOs, let the filter ring
steps.why:
Take VCO-1 out of the mixer and turn RESONANCE fully up.
- Mixer VCO-1 0 · 0%
- VCF RESONANCE 10 · 100%
- VCF FREQ 5.05 · 524 Hz
- Listen for: a pure whistle with every key at the same pitch.

steps.title: Play it in tune
steps.why:
KYBD CV at the top makes the cutoff follow the keys one to one.
- VCF KYBD CV or S/H MIXER 10 · 100%
- Listen for: the whistle playing the tune.

steps.title: Vibrato and a soft start
steps.why:
A little LFO sine on the cutoff, and a slower attack.
- VCF source (S/H or LFO) LFO sine
- VCF S/H or LFO 0.3 · 3%
- LFO FREQ 6 · 3.17 Hz
- AR ATTACK 3 · 40 ms
- AR RELEASE 4 · 160 ms
- Listen for: a theremin-like line that fades in and wavers.

context.vcf.resonance: SELF OSC: the filter is the sound.
context.vcf.mod1: Keyboard tracking, which keeps the whistle in tune.
context.vcf.freq: The whistle’s pitch at middle C.

tweaks.hear: A different, often weaker whistle from the 2-pole filter.
The sawtooth fighting the whistle: a squealing, unstable tone.

sounds.name: 2-Pole Brass
sounds.ref: Bright brass stabs that swell at the front through the gentler 2-pole filter, cut for disco horn lines
sounds.blurb: Bright brass stabs from the gentler 2-pole filter and a slow-opening envelope.
sounds.how: The 4023 filter at 2 poles lets more of the sawtooth through than the 4-pole ones: brighter and brassier. The ADSR opens it with a short attack, the swell at the front of a horn note, and also shapes the loudness.

steps.title: The 2-pole filter
steps.why:
Switch VCF MODE to the 4023 and bring in VCO-2, slightly detuned.
- VCF MODE 2-POLE (4023)
- Mixer VCO-2 8 · 80%
- VCO-2 FINE 5.5 · +0.2 st
- Listen for: a bright, thick pair of sawtooths.

steps.title: The swell
steps.why:
Lower the cutoff and let the ADSR open it with a short attack.
- VCF FREQ 4.5 · 358 Hz
- VCF ADSR or AR 6 · 60%
- ADSR ATTACK 3.5 · 56 ms
- ADSR DECAY 5 · 320 ms
- ADSR SUSTAIN 5 · 50%
- Listen for: each note blooming bright, as a horn does.

steps.title: The ADSR on the loudness
steps.why:
Switch the VCA to the ADSR too, with a short release.
- VCA envelope (AR or ADSR) ADSR
- ADSR RELEASE 3 · 110 ms
- Listen for: stabs that ease in and drop away, rather than switching on and off.

context.adsr.attack: The swell at the front of each stab.

tweaks.hear: A rounder, darker brass.
Slower, softer stabs.

sounds.name: Driven Pulse Bass
sounds.ref: A gritty, driven pulse bass with the boom trimmed off, for new-wave bass lines
sounds.blurb: A gritty pulse bass with DRIVE on and the boom taken out by the high-pass.
sounds.how: A narrowed pulse through the 4035 with resonance and a short envelope, then DRIVE for grit. The high-pass trims the lowest bass so the drive does not turn to mud.

steps.title: A narrow pulse
steps.why:
Switch VCO-1 to its pulse and narrow it.
- Mixer VCO-1 wave VCO-1 pulse
- VCO-1 PULSE WIDTH 4 · 32%
- Listen for: a thin, nasal tone.

steps.title: Pluck it
steps.why:
Close the 4035 with resonance and let the ADSR pluck it.
- VCF MODE 4-POLE (4035)
- VCF FREQ 3 · 127 Hz
- VCF RESONANCE 6 · 60%
- VCF ADSR or AR 5 · 50%
- ADSR DECAY 3 · 79 ms
- ADSR SUSTAIN 0 · 0%
- Listen for: short, squelchy bass notes.

steps.title: Drive, and trim the boom
steps.why:
Turn DRIVE on, and raise the high-pass a little.
- DRIVE on
- HPF CUTOFF FREQ 2 · 64 Hz
- Listen for: a louder, gritty bass that stays tight at the bottom.

context.hpf.cutoff: Keeps the lowest notes from going muddy.

tweaks.hear: The same line, cleaner and quieter.
A thin, telephone-like bass.

sounds.name: Laser Zap
sounds.ref: A zap that drops three octaves in an instant, the ray gun of 1970s science-fiction soundtracks
sounds.blurb: A falling zap: the ADSR throws VCO-1’s pitch up three octaves and lets it drop.
sounds.how: VCO-1’s second FM slider on the ADSR at near full raises its pitch by over three octaves at the start of a note; with no sustain the pitch falls straight back, in the decay time.

steps.title: Throw the pitch up
steps.why:
Switch VCO-1’s second FM slider to the ADSR and raise it nearly to the top. Take the sustain away.
- VCO-1 FM source (S/H or ADSR) ADSR
- VCO-1 FM (S/H or ADSR) 9 · 38.9 st
- ADSR DECAY 3.5 · 110 ms
- ADSR SUSTAIN 0 · 0%
- Listen for: a high pitch diving down to the note.

steps.title: A short tail
steps.why:
Lengthen the AR’s release a little.
- AR RELEASE 3 · 79 ms
- Listen for: each zap ending with a short fade.

context.vco1.fm2: How far up the pitch is thrown.

tweaks.hear: A slow, falling siren.
Random jumps instead of a fall.

sounds.name: LFO Square Trill
sounds.ref: A rapid trill a tone wide from a single key, a flourish of jazz-fusion synth solos
sounds.blurb: A rapid trill from one key: the LFO square flips VCO-1 between two pitches.
sounds.how: VCO-1’s first FM source switched to the LFO square jumps its pitch up and down instead of bending it. A small depth makes it a trill a tone wide.

steps.title: Square-wave FM
steps.why:
Switch VCO-1’s first FM source to the LFO square and raise the slider a little.
- VCO-1 FM source (LFO sine or square) LFO square
- VCO-1 FM (LFO) 2.9 · ±1 st
- LFO FREQ 7 · 5.02 Hz
- Listen for: the note flipping quickly between two pitches.

steps.title: Soften the tone
steps.why:
Lower the cutoff and add a little resonance.
- VCF FREQ 7 · 2.0 kHz
- VCF RESONANCE 3 · 30%
- Listen for: a rounder trill.

context.vco1.fm1_src: The square jumps the pitch where the sine would bend it.

tweaks.hear: A wider, wilder jump.
Vibrato instead of a trill.

sounds.name: Gain Drone
sounds.ref: Two detuned sawtooths that drone on with no key held while the filter drifts, for ambient pieces
sounds.blurb: A sound that never stops: VCA GAIN holds the amplifier open, and the LFO slowly moves the filter.
sounds.how: VCA GAIN opens the VCA with no key held, so the VCOs drone on. Two detuned sawtooths and a little pink noise go through a low cutoff, which the LFO sine sweeps very slowly.

steps.title: Hold the VCA open
steps.why:
Raise VCA GAIN: the sound plays with no key held.
- VCA GAIN 4 · 40%
- Listen for: a constant tone at middle C.

steps.title: Two sawtooths and some air
steps.why:
Lower VCO-1 a little, bring in VCO-2, detuned, and add a little pink noise.
- Mixer VCO-1 7 · 70%
- Mixer VCO-2 6 · 60%
- VCO-2 FINE 5.2 · +0.1 st
- NOISE or RING MOD 3 · 30%
- NOISE GEN PINK
- Listen for: a slowly beating drone with breath in it.

steps.title: Slow movement
steps.why:
Lower the cutoff and let the LFO sine sweep it slowly.
- VCF FREQ 4.5 · 358 Hz
- VCF source (S/H or LFO) LFO sine
- VCF S/H or LFO 3 · 30%
- LFO FREQ 1.5 · 0.40 Hz
- Listen for: the drone brightening and darkening over a few seconds.

context.vca.gain: Holds the amplifier open: the drone.
context.vcf.mod2: How far the slow LFO moves the cutoff.

tweaks.hear: Silence until a key is played.
A brighter, hissier breath.
